mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP by more than 1% over a quarter signals a contraction in economic demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 decreased by more than 1% over a quarter.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% over two months signals a strong supply-side expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 2% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST increased by more than 5% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and CPI inflation is rising, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates rise and economic growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate, signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS decreased by more than 100,000 and UNRATE increased.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales by more than 2% over a month signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate improved corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 70% of instances where RSAFS increased by more than 2% within a month.
